Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 1) Drug biotransformation means:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option2: Molecular alteration of drug in biological system
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option4: Drug movement from blood to tissue
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Biotransformation means chemical or molecular alteration of drug. It usually occurs inside biological systems. It is also called drug metabolism.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 2) The main organ of drug biotransformation is:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Liver is the main organ of drug biotransformation. It contains many drug-metabolizing enzymes. Other organs may also contribute.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 3) An extrahepatic site of drug biotransformation is:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Intestinal mucosa can metabolize some drugs. Lung, kidney, adrenal glands and skin may also contribute. Liver remains the major site.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 4) The main aim of biotransformation is to convert lipophilic drugs into:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Biotransformation usually makes drugs more polar. Polar compounds are more easily excreted. Renal and biliary excretion become easier.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 5) Biotransformation generally helps drug removal by:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Metabolism makes many drugs more water-soluble. Water-soluble compounds are easier to excrete. Kidney and bile are important elimination routes.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 6) A prodrug becomes active after:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Prodrug has little or no action before conversion. Biotransformation activates it inside the body. Levodopa and carbimazole are examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 7) Phase I reaction is mainly:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phase I reaction is functionalization or catabolic reaction. It introduces or exposes functional groups. It may prepare drug for Phase II conjugation.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 8) Phase II reaction is mainly:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phase II reaction is conjugation. It is usually anabolic and energy-requiring. It generally produces polar inactive conjugates.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 9) Phase I reaction may cause drug activity to be:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phase I reaction may inactivate, activate or not change activity. It mainly prepares drug for conjugation or excretion. The effect varies by drug.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 10) Phase II reaction usually produces:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phase II reaction usually produces inactive polar conjugates. These are readily excretable. Kidney and bile are common routes.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 11) Compared with Phase I, Phase II reaction generally requires:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phase II reaction is energy-requiring. It uses conjugating molecules. The final product is usually polar and excretable.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 12) Phase I reaction mainly includes oxidation, reduction and:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phase I reactions include oxidation, reduction and hydrolysis. They are functionalization reactions. Conjugation reactions belong to Phase II.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 13) Oxidation means:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option2: Removal of oxygen or addition of hydrogen
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option4: Addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Oxidation adds oxygen or removes hydrogen. It is a Phase I reaction. Phenytoin, phenobarbital and propranolol are examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 14) Reduction means:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option2: Removal of oxygen or addition of hydrogen
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Reduction removes oxygen or adds hydrogen. It is a Phase I reaction. Chloramphenicol and methadone are examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 15) Hydrolysis means:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Hydrolysis breaks a compound by adding water. It is a Phase I reaction. Procaine and succinylcholine are ester examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 16) Procaine and succinylcholine undergo:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Procaine and succinylcholine are ester examples. They undergo hydrolysis. Hydrolysis is a Phase I reaction.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 17) Lidocaine and procainamide are examples of drugs undergoing hydrolysis of:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Lidocaine and procainamide are amide examples. They undergo hydrolysis. Ester examples include procaine and succinylcholine.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 18) Phenytoin, phenobarbital and propranolol are examples of:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: These drugs are examples of oxidation. Oxidation adds oxygen or removes hydrogen. It belongs to Phase I metabolism.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 19) Chloramphenicol and methadone are examples of:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Chloramphenicol and methadone are examples of reduction. Reduction removes oxygen or adds hydrogen. It is a Phase I reaction.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 20) Glucuronidation is catalyzed by:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Glucuronidation uses UDP-glucuronyl transferase. It is a Phase II conjugation reaction. Aspirin and morphine are examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 21) Aspirin and morphine commonly undergo:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Aspirin and morphine are examples of glucuronidation. This is a Phase II reaction. It usually increases polarity and excretion.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 22) Acetylation is catalyzed by:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Acetylation is mediated by N-acetyltransferase. It is a Phase II reaction. Isoniazid and dapsone are examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 23) Isoniazid and dapsone undergo:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Isoniazid and dapsone are examples of acetylation. Acetylation is a Phase II reaction. It is catalyzed by N-acetyltransferase.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 24) Methylation is catalyzed by:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Methylation is catalyzed by transmethylase. Adrenaline and dopamine are examples. It is a Phase II reaction.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 25) Adrenaline and dopamine are examples of:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Adrenaline and dopamine undergo methylation. Methylation uses transmethylase. It belongs to Phase II metabolism.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 26) Sulfation is catalyzed by:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Sulfation is catalyzed by sulfotransferase. It is a Phase II reaction. Paracetamol and methyldopa are examples.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 27) Paracetamol and methyldopa may undergo:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Paracetamol and methyldopa are examples of sulfation. Sulfation is a conjugation reaction. It increases polarity.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 28) Glutathione conjugation is especially important for:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Paracetamol undergoes glutathione conjugation. This pathway is important in overdose toxicity. Depletion of glutathione increases hepatic injury risk.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 29) Glycine conjugation is seen with:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Salicylates undergo glycine conjugation. This is a Phase II reaction. It is catalyzed by acyl-CoA glycine transferase.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 30) Enzyme induction causes:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Enzyme induction increases drug-metabolizing enzyme activity. This increases metabolism of concomitant drugs. It may cause therapeutic failure or interactions.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 31) Enzyme inhibition causes:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Enzyme inhibition decreases metabolism of concomitant drugs. This may increase drug effect and toxicity. It can also reduce activation of prodrugs.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 32) A consequence of enzyme induction is:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Induction can increase metabolism of active drugs. This may lower plasma level and cause therapeutic failure. It may also increase toxicity of active metabolites.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 33) Which is an enzyme inducer?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Rifampicin is a classic enzyme inducer. It increases metabolism of many drugs. This can reduce efficacy of concomitant therapy.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 34) Which is an enzyme inducer?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Carbamazepine is an enzyme inducer. It can increase metabolism of other drugs. Rifampicin, phenytoin and barbiturates are also inducers.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 35) Which is an enzyme inducer?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Phenytoin is an enzyme inducer. It may reduce levels of other drugs. It also has important monitoring concerns.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 36) Which is an enzyme inducer?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Griseofulvin is an enzyme inducer. It increases metabolism of concomitant drugs. This may lead to reduced therapeutic effect.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 37) Which is an enzyme inhibitor?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Cimetidine is an enzyme inhibitor. It decreases metabolism of several drugs. This may increase drug effect or toxicity.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 38) Which is an enzyme inhibitor?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Ketoconazole is an enzyme inhibitor. It can increase levels of drugs metabolized by hepatic enzymes. Fluconazole is also an inhibitor.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 39) Which is an enzyme inhibitor?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Sodium valproate is an enzyme inhibitor. It may raise levels of some concomitant drugs. Drug interaction risk becomes important.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 40) Which is an enzyme inhibitor?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Ciprofloxacin is an enzyme inhibitor. It may increase effects or toxicity of drugs metabolized by inhibited enzymes. Monitoring may be needed in combinations.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 41) Enzyme inhibition may cause therapeutic failure when the affected drug is a:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Some prodrugs need metabolism for activation. Enzyme inhibition may reduce their conversion to active form. This may cause therapeutic failure despite adequate dosing.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 42) A prodrug is best defined as a drug that:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option1: Produces little or no effect until chemically altered
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Prodrug is inactive or weakly active initially. It becomes active after chemical alteration in the body. This can improve absorption, distribution or tolerability.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 43) Cortisone is converted to:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Cortisone is a prodrug of hydrocortisone. This conversion activates the therapeutic moiety. It is an example of prodrug activation.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 44) Talampicillin and bacampicillin are converted to:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Talampicillin and bacampicillin are converted to ampicillin. They are prodrug examples. This modification improves absorption and distribution.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 45) Dipivefrin is converted to:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Dipivefrin is converted to adrenaline. It is designed to improve delivery and tolerability. Prodrug design may improve bioavailability.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 46) Levodopa is converted to:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Levodopa is converted to dopamine. Dopamine itself poorly enters the brain. Levodopa is used to deliver dopamine effect after conversion.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 47) Carbimazole is converted to:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Carbimazole is converted to methimazole. Methimazole is the active antithyroid drug. This is a standard prodrug example.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 48) Sulfasalazine is converted to:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Sulfasalazine is converted to 5-aminosalicylic acid. This releases the active moiety inside the body. It is used in inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatologic conditions.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 49) Drug excretion means:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.option3: Removal of drug or metabolites from body
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Excretion removes drug and metabolites from the body. It is the final elimination process. Kidney is the major route.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 50) The main channel of drug excretion is:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Kidney is the main channel of drug excretion. Renal excretion is especially important for water-soluble drugs. Renal impairment can increase toxicity.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 51) Which is a route of drug excretion?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Bile can excrete drugs and metabolites. Some drugs undergo enterohepatic cycling after biliary excretion. Kidney remains the main excretory organ.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 52) Which substance may carry excreted drug and is important in lactation caution?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Some drugs are excreted in breast milk. This may expose the infant during breastfeeding. Drug choice in lactation should consider infant safety.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 53) Which drug is excreted in breast milk?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Ampicillin may be excreted in breast milk. Other listed examples include aspirin and diazepam. Infant exposure should be considered during lactation.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 54) Which drug is listed among drugs excreted in breast milk?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Diazepam may be excreted in breast milk. Sedation risk in the infant should be considered. Breastfeeding drug safety depends on dose, duration and infant age. Long-acting sedatives need extra caution.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 55) Which drug is excreted in breast milk?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Tetracycline may be excreted in breast milk. The degree of infant risk depends on exposure and duration. Drug selection during lactation should balance maternal benefit and infant safety. Safer alternatives are preferred when suitable.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 56) Which opioid is listed among drugs excreted in breast milk?
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Morphine may be excreted in breast milk. Opioids can potentially sedate the infant. Dose, duration and infant monitoring are important. Short courses may differ from chronic use in risk assessment.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 57) Renal excretion of many drugs involves filtration, secretion and:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Renal handling includes glomerular filtration, tubular secretion and tubular reabsorption. Only free drug is filtered at the glomerulus. Secretion can actively move drugs into tubules. Reabsorption depends on lipid solubility and urine pH.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 58) Urinary alkalinization enhances excretion of:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Weak acids become more ionized in alkaline urine. Ionized drug is less reabsorbed from renal tubule. This enhances urinary excretion by ion trapping. Salicylate poisoning is a classic application.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 59) Urinary acidification enhances excretion of:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Weak bases become more ionized in acidic urine. Ionized molecules remain trapped in tubular fluid. This can enhance renal elimination. However, deliberate urinary acidification is rarely used clinically because of safety concerns.

Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.question: 60) Enterohepatic circulation may prolong drug action because drug excreted in bile can be:
Bio transformation,Enzyme induction and.exp: Some drugs are excreted in bile and reach intestine. They may be deconjugated and reabsorbed. This enterohepatic recycling prolongs drug action. It can also produce secondary peaks in plasma concentration.
